html:
The Katyn massacre was the killing of about 22,000 Polish prisoners, most of them officers, police and educated reservists, by the Soviet secret police in spring 1940, in the Katyn forest near Smolensk and elsewhere.

They had been captured when the Soviet Union invaded eastern Poland in September 1939. Stalin and the Politburo ordered them shot. Germany found the graves in 1943 and announced it, and the Soviets blamed the Germans, a lie the Western Allies did not challenge. When the Polish government in exile asked for an inquiry, Moscow broke off relations. Only in 1990 did Gorbachev's government admit Soviet guilt. In 2010 a plane carrying Poland's president and many leaders to a memorial service crashed near Smolensk, killing all aboard. It remains central to how Poland remembers the war.
sum: The Katyn massacre was the killing of about 22,000 Polish prisoners, most of them officers, police and educated reservists, by the Soviet secret police in spring 1940, in the Katyn forest near Smolensk and elsewhere.
